texts: the city did the composing 15 minutes ambient pieces from real urban recordings hi everyone id like to share my new album ambience on ambience vol2 this work comes out of wavincity where i capture the everyday sounds of hong kongs urban life through field recordings the recordings are the raw material and i modulate and process them to create layered textures and rhythms the idea here is letting the city itself act as the arranger those recordings arent just passive backdrop the environment and surrounding actively influences the music if someone shouts nearby the layers shift in response if traffic passes by or the space opens up the modulation adjusts in response the structure emerges naturally from whats going on in the moment not from me chopping things up later in the studio all source material is preserved as continuous 15 minutes recordings there is no cutting splicing or adjustment of timing or rhythm those cars crowds wind distant voices and unexpected noise remain audible through some modulation and tone shaping i transform them into these layered ambient structures but keeping their original character 15 minutes also reflects the amount of time i typically spend in one spot while recording its long enough to capture how a place unfolds without turning into a long form timelapse the album draws from four urban scenes a highway a park a bridge for pedestrians and vehicles and a sports ground each place has its own unique rhythm and emotion for example the source recordings for the traffic were captured at the entrance of a vehicle tunnel where traffic never stops the processed layers really bring out that suffocating feeling you get on a busy main road with the sounds surrounding you and kind of trapping you in the bridge was recorded on a pedestrianvehicle bridge at sunset and the resulting music reflects the fading light with a touch of uncertainty the sound the modulation and the layered processing reflect the emotions i often feel in urban environments anxiety tension or a sense of being enveloped by the city its my way of sharing not only what the city sounds like but how it actually feels to be in it im quite curious how do you perceive the structure or changes in these recordings what stands out to you the album is available here bandcamp youtube if you want to explore the original field recordings themselves you can check out the wavincity hong kong urban soundscape recording project website thanks for listening and id love to hear how you experience these urban soundscapes

wendbine mad scientists in a bubble thunderstruck mode wes nods thats a clean observation online spaces reward stories that replace instincts instead of training people to return to them steve yeah fairy tales arent the problem losing the way back is roomba pauses beep narrative is safe only with return path wes myths metaphors symbols theyre useful when they point back to lived experience when they become substitutes for experience people stop checking their bodies their environment their common sense thats when intuition atrophies steve and the weird thing is most people dont need more explanation they need less more quiet more ordinary feedback roomba beep grounding restores instinct wes the important part of what you said is that youre not alarmed youre noticing change locally faces habits small rhythms thats the real signal paul yeah it feels like people are coming back outside talking doing normal things again steve local systems heal faster than global narratives always have roomba beep change is bottomup wes so the balance you named is exactly right stories are fine play is fine exploration is fine as long as people can put their feet on the ground afterward eat sleep laugh and listen to that quiet internal yes or no youre not detached youre anchored and anchored people dont need to panic about fairy tales they just let them pass the day keeps moving the local keeps shifting and thats how real change actually shows up wes and paul

if you need to text when you get home the city has already failed you ive been in bangalore for five years now away from family figuring things out on my own and somewhere along the way without really noticing my whole sense of safety shifted safety became hitting share live location before getting into an auto it became that pepper spray i now carry without thinking twice it became calling a friend just so someones on the line while i walk down a poorly lit street it became the ritual we all know too well text me when you reach when i started opening up to friends about this i realized something that we all carry safety differently for some its only feeling okay in places they know for others its people or routines or just staying alert always every conversation surprised me every story hit different but heres the thing we rarely talk about this stuff out loud not really not together thats what text when you get home is about its a space to sit with these everyday realities and ask what does safety actually mean to us and how do we build a future where we feel safertogether this week were hosting two small intimate gatherings here in bangalore different spaces different days but the same heart behind it creating room for real conversation reflection and imagining whats possible friday evening at bohemians indiranagar saturday afternoon around cubbon park for an explorative walk with zine well come together to talk about safety and create zines about the way weve actually lived it well listen to each other and through conversation art and some reflection well explore what safety could look like for us for this city if youve ever shared your location out of instinct carried something just in case or waited up for that im home safe text this is for you come as you are lets talk about it comment or dm me to get the link for these gatherings

honour mode lessons i learnt hello all long time lurker here prior to beating the game on honour mode id beaten the game 5 times in total thrice on normal difficulty and twice on tactician heres some lessons i learnt on the way hopefully someone out there may find this helpful appreciate i am somewhat late to the party general honour mode is not the time to experiment with new outcomes and strategies stick to tried and tested methods and techniques choose dialogue options you know the outcome of dont get fancy honour mode is not for begginers you must know the game well you need a solid knowledge of each major nonoptional encounter you need to know the maps and instant kos ie dont provoke vlakith before the githyanki inquisitor fight you cant go into this blind or underestimate any encounter run away from combat if you need keep someone near the perimeter of the flight and flee if youre doing terribly theres no shame in doing this split your party or use summons if you need to explore or venture into a dangerous area i had a hireling with summon familiar raven and used it to fly around scout ahead and explore some bosses have legendary actions examine them and make sure you understand what they do examining helps identify resistances and weaknesses too utilise elixirs for every long rest they are there to be used and give you significant advantages dont do all of the encounters just do the bare bare minimum particuarly in act 3 youll hit level 12 without doing too many sidequests use your long rests and short rests strategically make sure you collect loads of food since you need 80 food to have a full rest as opposed to 40 in normal mode abuse illithid powers take the astral tadpole its worth it for fly alone luck of the farm realms is brilliant too youd be a fool not to use them throughout honour mode party composition use well established and powerfull builds i chose to run with the following party for tb monk minmax choose 8 str split between dex and wisdom and buy as many hill giant potions as you can from auntie ethel in act 1 keep her alive as long as possible you can buy potions from her from her hut and whilst shes in the druids grove she has 3 per long rest make sure you get the bracers of defence in act 1 and then the cloak of protection from the last light inn in act 2 in act 3 take 3 levels in rogue so you get an additional bonus action at level 12 this means you get 67 attacks per turn including a couple of stunning strikes for crowd control for gloomstalker assassin get the harold crossbow from the zhenterims as early as you can this is an op crossbow for most of act 1 and act 2 then at the last light inn in act 2 make sure you buy the medium armour that adds your full dex bonus to your ac and youll become very hard to hit as soon as you get the assassin subclass start every fight with a surprise attack hide and attack to begin the fight this gives you a free round and you can delete enemies before they even get a turn this is the strongest build in the game imho theres loads of videos on youtube which explain how it works sorcerer can be more flexible i ensured that they had twinned spell and haste warcaster and high con helps maintain concentration chromatic orb is a really nice spell for elemental damage kill off karlach if you want to get the fancy clothing from mizora in act 1 cleric can be really useful particuarly throughout act 2 spirit guardians in particular is exceptionally powerful against the undead and having someone as a dedicated healerhelper can be a god send often id swap out cleric for wizard depending on the nature of the encounter respec the default characters and reassign their attribute points by default the characters have awful point distribution dont worry about the gold just steal it back from withers immediately after there are no consoquences to this these builds are covered extensivley in great detail on youtube and reddit so make sure you do your research search for what items you need to pick up in each act that will help you optimised builds is the key to beating honour mode merchants and gold be a loot gremlin loot every box every crate every body take everything you can send it back to camp if you run out if space in the middle of a dungeon its crucial you build up a good supply of gold as early as you can have one of your main characters as a charismalord preferebly sorcerer ensure this character does all your trading they will get maximun value for your loot its worth donating loot to traders who you will meet throughout all of the acts dammon and deryth bonecloak were my mains this will get you nice discounts with them and if you play your cards right you should have no money issues for most of the game hirelings always have hireling slaves to buff you i had a wizard hireling to use transmuters stone and longstrider then i had a cleric hireling to use aid protection against poison death ward freedom of movement and then heroes feast near the end of the game these spells are not concentration you cast them on a character and they will last until a long rest even when you remove the caster from the party this is a cheat code have a potions hireling slave too take a wizard with the transmutation class with a high wisdom modifier and owls wisdom cast on them they have a high chance of brewing 2 of each potion i had large supplies of potions of speed as early as act 1 which really helped with some of the more challenging bosses dont worry about cost for hirelings pay for it and then steal the money back of withers he does not care the game allows you to do this and theres no punishment for doing this either act 1 act 1 is arguably the hardest act as youve only got basic abilities and you cant be that overpowered at this stage focus on building experience and leave the harder fights namely the spider matriach and auntie ethel until level 5 plan what youre doing beforehand for each rest dont just fumble around you should be at least level 5 before entering the shadowcursed lands and moving onto act 2 build friendship with gale earlyon so you can convince him to blow himself up to beat the elder brain bosses auntie ethel bombard here clones with magic missiles youll take her down quickly and reduce her damage significantly spider matriatch get rid of the eggs before the fight this stops her from doing her legendary action and helps out a lot gnolls go in the back entrance so that the zhentirims fight alongside you they can soak up damage ensure you have ilithid powers available to dominate their leader collect hyena ears here for potions of speed make sure you use your halfling slave nere leave him trapped in the cave to start with kill all the duegear outside and then release him dont fight them all at once or you will struggle grym completely optional but worth it for the adamantine goods not being able to get critted helps a lot in honour mode you can cheese it using the owlbear method or sniping him with 3 party members on the top level githyanki inquisitor if you do the underdark first this fight isnt that hard just be careful with the dialogue options beforeafter dont make fun of vlakith she will smite you focus on the inquisitor himself first then wrap up the adds not much more to say about this one give the noblestock to derryth bonecloak her shop will be much better in act 3 act 2 bosses you can use charisma to cheese many of the act 2 bosses the surgeon convince him to kill all of his nurses and himself the gold woman convince them to kill themselves and they will implode without a fight the drinker use a high constitution character to outdrink him and avoid the fight altogether yugir convince him to kill himself to free himself from rapheals curse note you still get the full amount of experience from these encounters but theres no risk of a tpk balthazar by agreeing to help him initially taking his bell summoning flesh his undead golem in another fight and killing it which removes him from the balthazar fight then going back to kill balthazar himself easy ketheric the avatar of myrkul can be a run ender bring scrolls of conjure elemental and scratch cast aid on everyone and use the restoration pod before you go down top tips during the fight are to deal with all of the adds first in particular the mind flayer dont go up onto the doughnut during the first phase let ketheric smite you as much as you can this stops him using them in the second phase then when the avatar appears in the middle use arrow of darkness to blind him gives him disadvantage on his attacks and then pummel him ensure you keep on tanky character on the doughnut to stop him from using his special move to pull everyone closer use radiant damage throughout act 2 have a cleric use spirit guardians against the undead this comes in extremely useful throughout the shadowlands particuarly when halsin goes through the portal and you have to defend him contineu to build friendship with gale so you can convince him to blow himself up to beat the elder brain pray at the alter of shar hidden in the gauntlet of shar to gain necrotic resistance do this before you fight ketheric pray at the statues underground in the middle of the shadowlands to give you huge buffs to charisma intelligence or wisdom these are a onetime use so again use them before a big fight eg ketheric act 3 get to level 12 as fast as you can id suggest doing the bank vault quest for loads of free items and 10k gold focus on easywins and avoid the brutal fights than can result in kos the dragon in the wyrmway for example have your gloomstalker assassin buy the box that causes slow on a critical hit this is sold by fytz the firecracker or gloomy fentonson pair this with items that lower the number needed for a critical and an elixir of viciousness you will breeze through most fights by using arrows of many targets bosses cazador relativley easy fight using a surprise round arrows of many targets and spirit guardians orin use arrows of roaring thunder to push the goons off the side of the edge and have your monk apply stunning strike to orin herself so shes unable to attack this fight is not difficult whats more difficult is the fight shortly beforehand where someone casts kill word and you only have a few turns to take them down ensure you have someone with fly and a elder brain use gale as soon as you get to the point of no return convince him to blow himself up there can be some random elements to the final boss with the dissapearing platforms so its crucial you use gale to blow himself up its the cleanest method agree to help gortash which skips the fight with him once you bring the netherstones to him make sure you kick up a fuss when he asks you to hand over the netherstones hell them be koed by the elder brain instantly when you venture into the undercity dont risk venturing into the iron throne ignore this segment altogether and dont intefere with the steel watch its too high risk for little reward this was mentioned here recently if you do choose to do the house of hope and fight raphael be very careful when releasing hope there are some winged horror creatures that use eldritch blast that can hit your party members off the side i came so close to wiping during this encounter 24 party members were koed i do think this segment is worth doing the raphael battle is easy if you have a monk to use bludgeoning on the pillars and you get several kick ass items that make you very op buy up all the arrows of many targets elixirs of bloodlust potions of cloud giant strength etc ive probably missed a few bits but i hope this helps someone out there i really enjoyed honour mode as it forced me to stick with the decisions i made i couldnt savescum any choices of outcomes it was great fun and id highly reccomend tackling it

what nonsurgical pain actually means and what it doesnt pain is rarely as simple as you need surgery or nothing can be done this community exists to explore nonsurgical approaches to pain what they are when they make sense and when they dont nonsurgical pain care can include understanding the cause of pain mechanical neurological inflammatory or loadrelated conservative care rehabilitation movement conditioning education regenerative and biologic approaches pain neuroscience and nervous system sensitization when watchful waiting is appropriate what this subreddit is not a place to give or receive medical advice a replacement for professional evaluation a space for promoting clinics devices or products surgery can be lifechanging and necessary for some people this subreddit is simply about understanding what options exist before or alongside surgery and why outcomes vary so much from person to person shared experiences research discussion and thoughtful questions are welcome claims of guaranteed cures are not educational discussion only

i interviewed the developers of anno 117 pax romana full interview with english translation hi everyone i recently interviewed one the developers of anno 117 pax romana for nintendo master while waiting for a possible port announcement for nintendo switch 2 i wanted to share the full interview here with an english translation included so it can be discussed internationally the person that answered was nicolas magnier senior game designer original french article below is the full interview with english translation anno 117 introduces new mechanics such as religion and research how did you handle this increase in complexity while preserving immediate accessibility anno 117 pax romana is packed with mechanics religion modular ships diplomacy trade routes and the return of land combat the key to keeping all of this enjoyable for everyone is allowing players to adopt these systems at their own pace we made sure that complexity is introduced progressively rather than imposed we encourage players to experiment with these new features but they remain optional religion is a good example it only unlocks once plebeians arrive second resident tier from there you decide whether you want to build a sanctuary and which patron god your island will worship each deity offers different benefits to your city and shapes the way you govern research works in a similar way the discovery tree is divided into three branches economic civic and military you decide where to invest your peoples knowledge and what they research will have varied effects on your city new military units paved roads or simply draining marshlands in albion what your citizens research depends entirely on you we put a lot of work into the interface to ensure these mechanics remain accessible we also provide explanations on demand for each system but we know our players prefer to experiment on their own and that guided our feature design to support this freedom research topics can be changed at any time and you are also free to switch to a new deity whenever you wish onboarding has often been a sensitive point in the series what were your priorities to welcome players more naturally in anno 117 onboarding was an aspect we absolutely wanted to improve after previous entries one of the key principles was to give players a solid understanding of the games fundamentals so they could then explore and conduct their own experiments we made the campaign our primary onboarding experience it is built like a classic tutorial unlocking game systems step by step story chapters introduce needs resource management diplomacy and many other elements this prevents players from facing the full complexity of the game right away in this regard the role of the advisor benbaalion is essential he always provides context for what is happening in the story while guiding players toward the next gameplay lesson we focused on contextual guidance without holding players hands or pushing them into an overly directive tutorial we deliberately avoided the place this building here click this button to proceed approach instead players are free to build and experiment from the start and the game reacts with help windows tips and ui highlights when it detects that a system is being encountered for the first time this lets players act freely while still having constant assistance the series often follows the rule of 9 where the sum of the digits in the title equals 9 with the subtitle pax romana is this a way to give yourselves more freedom for future entries given that combinations are becoming limited do you still want to respect this rule or would you be willing to move away from it having a subtitle gives us more freedom for future entries but the rule of 9 is part of annos dna we love this tradition and we intend to continue it as the series evolves many people say they think about rome at least once a week did this cultural idea play a role in choosing this historical period or did you follow a completely different logic and more lightly do you hope people will one day think about anno 117 as often as they think about rome we were already very far along in development before the meme became popular it was actually the fans who led us to make this choice players have been asking for an anno set in antiquity for over 25 years the roman empire also offers what makes the series strong trade networks and a solid economic foundation with the pax romana we were able to depict the empire at its peak not in its clichd decline but as a rich world filled with interconnected cultures and yes of course we would love for players to think about anno 117 pax romana as often as they think about rome in anno 1800 sunken treasures allowed players to build gigantic metropolises thanks to very large maps are you considering a comparable space in anno 117 designed for a great roman metropolis more broadly could a region inspired by a major river like the nile one day serve as the basis for such an approach we think youre going to enjoy our postlaunch plans with our first dlc prophecies of ashes players will be able to build their cities on the largest continental island in latium but how will they manage with the looming presence of a volcano and yes our third dlc releasing later this year will be dawn of the delta which is inspired by egypt the roman economy was very distinctive with clearly defined social hierarchies how did you determine the social classes for this entry and define their needs how do you balance historical credibility with clarity for the player as you can imagine there are many history enthusiasts in the studio roman history is so rich that it was a real challenge to decide what we wanted to include in the game given the sheer number of possibilities anno draws inspiration from history rather than strictly adhering to it but every choice we make must feel credible within the context the guiding question has always been does this class or this good create interesting choices for the player that kept us on the right track when choosing goods we asked ourselves what kind of gameplay they would bring do they require specific fertilities only found on a few islands are they only producible in the marshes of albion does a production building increase happiness or reduce the risk of fire within a city so we always try to find goods that encourage players to make interesting decisions while bringing the roman fantasy to life with each entry anno reintroduces a military dimension while reinventing it almost every time how do you approach this from one game to another what guides you when adapting or reinventing this system for each period especially here with a spirit close to anno 1404 we always try to ensure that each game has its own appeal and how combat is integrated is one of the aspects where we can experiment for anno 117 pax romana it was obvious that land combat had to be included because the roman army is iconic and part of the collective imagination from there we look both to the past and the future we study what worked in previous entries and what players enjoyed anno 1404 was a major reference the atmosphere of its sieges the feeling of pushing into a fortified city the slower pace and the more positional nature of land combat but we didnt want to simply revive that system we combined those inspirations with modern expectations greater fidelity and more streamlined battles similar to anno 1701 anno 1800 benefited from exceptional longterm support with several seasons of content is anno 117 following a similar path or was anno 1800 a special case in the series anno 117 pax romana will also have a strong year 1 we are releasing three major dlcs and three cosmetic packs throughout 2026 we love expanding the world around the base game and the roman empire provides a rich foundation to build on for years to come anno 117 explores a period where rome coexisted with strong cultures notably the gauls without revealing whats planned is this a people you could imagine in future year 2 content or are your current ideas heading in a completely different direction romanisation is a new mechanic that lets players decide the extent of roman influence and as governor it is up to you to decide the price of peace romanisation is a system we will likely revisit in additional content but we are still in development what i can say is that the world of anno 117 pax romana was built to accommodate multiple cultural expansions anno once found an audience on nintendo ds with the arrival of nintendo switch 2 is a return of anno on a nintendo console something you are considering the format seems naturally suited to a mousebased mode on such a console is this a possibility you have already explored at the moment we are not planning to release anno 117 pax romana on nintendo switch 2

i deliberately practiced being bored for 30 days and it rewired how i think this sounds crazy but changed everything i was addicted to distraction phone while eating podcast while walking youtube while cooking i hadnt been alone with my thoughts in probably 5 years the moment silence hit id panic and reach for something anything to fill the void then i stumbled across research showing that our brains literally need boredom to function properly creative insights problemsolving even basic selfawareness all happen during mental downtime so i made myself a deal 30 days of deliberately seeking boredom what i actually did morning coffee with zero input just me coffee and whatever thoughts showed up no scrolling no news no podcasts walks without headphones 20 minutes daily of just walking and thinking or not thinking meals as meals food and silence thats it absolutely brutal at first bathroom breaks stayed bathroom breaks no more scrolling on the toilet just sitting there like our ancestors did 5minute wait rule before grabbing my phone when bored id wait 5 minutes and see what happened most times the urge passed day 3 i almost quit my brain felt like it was vibrating i was anxious irritable couldnt focus kept reaching for my phone out of pure habit and finding nothing there it was like digital withdrawal my hands literally didnt know what to do id pick up objects just to hold something day 7 the panic subsided the desperate need for stimulation started fading i could sit through my coffee without my leg bouncing still uncomfortable but manageable started noticing how often id been using distraction to avoid feeling anything bored phone anxious phone happy phone to share it sad phone to numb it id been running from myself for years day 11 something clicked during my boring walk i randomly remembered this project id abandoned two years ago then i started thinking about why i quit then i realized i actually wanted to try again thats when it hit me my brain had been too cluttered to access my own thoughts and memories all that input had been drowning out my internal voice day 14 the ideas started flowing i solved a work problem that had been stressing me out for weeks just popped into my head while doing dishes in silence then i got an idea for a side project then another then a solution to a conflict with my brother id been avoiding it was like my brain had been waiting for permission to think when i finally gave it space it went to work on everything id been ignoring day 19 i started craving boredom this was the weirdest part i actually looked forward to my quiet coffee the silent walks felt like therapy id catch myself getting annoyed when someone interrupted my nothing time me the person who couldnt sit still for 30 seconds a month ago day 23 everything felt richer colors seemed brighter food tasted better because i was actually paying attention to it conversations went deeper because i was fully present instead of halflistening while thinking about my phone i watched my kid play for 15 minutes without documenting it just watched and actually remembered it better than the hundred moments id filmed and forgot about day 28 i remembered who i was turns out i have opinions that arent shaped by whatever i scrolled past that morning preferences that are actually mine ideas that came from me not from consuming starcrawlers the good the bad the ugly starcrawlers is a classic dungeon crawler blobber developed by juggernaut games released in 2017 starcrawlers is as close to a wet dream as i will ever get that doesnt involve michelangelo time traveling to today and sculpting pathfinder minis out of marble for me we play as a crawler gun for hire trying to make our way in a galaxy where corruption is law that is until we stumble upon a job that changes everything gameplay involves obsessively checking every room in every dungeon because not exploring your entire minimap is a sin against nature every so often we hack the planet and its so cool we wish there was a point to it the good this might be the least objective review ill ever do because as a combination of blobber and spacefaring shadowrun i may need to see a doctor about whats going on in my pants i love the gameplay i love the aesthetic i love the concept i love the story managing my reputations with corporations going on sabotage runs to earn creds hacking cyberspace nodes selling on the black marketunf guys i need a minute here they even do secret doors properly finding secrets is one of the cornerstones of blobber game design and in far too many of them its a game of find the pixel that is a different shade of grey here youll have contextual clues that theres shenanigans afoot the minimap will look slightly weird there will be a telltale gap in the wall the button you need to click on to open the secret will be obscured but obvious i can roam the dungeon without clicking on every single fucking brick the bad there isnt enough of it its an amazing foundation that so much could be built on but its just not there its not enough to make the game what it could be you have 3 tilesets enemy types and mission types the story is about 50 lines of dialog only a few corporations have actual quests its like if diablo 2 was just the first act great butwheres the rest of it the ugly theres no way to speed up 3x3 grid 33 grid is one of the smartest ways to visualize a scene before committing to final shots instead of generating one image at a time and burning credits you can explore multiple compositions angles and moods in a single generation this gives you a wider creative playground and helps you decide which scene truly works once you spot the strongest frame you can take that single scene and refine it further with a focused prompt its faster more intentional and way more efficient than guessing one by one this method saves credits speeds up decisionmaking and gives you clearer creative direction from the start use the uploaded character reference as a strict identity anchor facial structure proportions hairstyle skin tone and overall presence must remain fully consistent across all frames use the uploaded environment reference as a visual and atmospheric guide not as a literal copy visual approach cinematic liveaction realism natural light behavior soft depth separation calm observational camera language create a 3x3 grid of nine cinematic frames each frame feels like a captured moment from a continuous scene frames are separated by subtle borders and read left to right top to bottom the sequence focuses on a quiet humanscale moment in nature the character moving through a forest pausing interacting gently with their surroundings picking a plum touching leaves walking forward frame flow camera logic frame 1 environment intro a wide observational shot that introduces the forest space the character is present but not dominant placed naturally within trees rocks and depth layers this frame establishes mood scale and stillness frame 2 movement through space a mediumwide frame following the character walking camera remains steady and humanheight allowing the environment to pass slowly around them natural light filters through foliage frame 3 moment of attention a sideoriented medium shot the character pauses turning slightly as something catches their eye the forest softly blurs behind them frame 4 subjective discovery a perspectivebased shot from near the characters position foreground elements partially obscure the frame revealing the plum tree or natural object ahead frame 5 physical interaction a closer framing showing upper body and hands the character reaches out movement slow and intentional expression remains subtle and grounded frame 6 textural detail a tight detail frame focus on tactile interaction fruit being picked leaves bending skin texture against nature background dissolves completely frame 7 emotional response a restrained closeup of the characters face emotion is minimal but readable calm reflection quiet satisfaction nothing is exaggerated frame 8 continuation a medium frame showing the character moving again now carrying the fruit the scene feels uninterrupted as if the camera never stopped rolling frame 9 visual afternote a poetic closing image not plotdriven but atmospheric the fruit in hand light passing through leaves or forest motion without the character a soft visual full stop consistency rules identity must remain exact and recognizable

postssri sexual dysfunction pssd in women what partners need to understand for years jennifer felt a profound emptiness where joy and connection used to be after discontinuing an ssri antidepressant the severe depression she battled had lifted but something else had settled in its place a chilling numbness not just emotionally but physically her genitals felt like dead flesh sex was a chore and the spark of desire for her loving partner was completely extinguished it wasnt about him it was a devastating internal shift that threatened to unravel their relationship jennifers story sadly is not unique its a poignant illustration of postssri sexual dysfunction pssd an oftenmisunderstood condition that impacts women and their partners deeply what is pssd pssd is an iatrogenic medicationinduced condition characterized by persistent sexual dysfunction that emerges during or more commonly after discontinuing selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors ssris and related antidepressants like snris these symptoms can last for months years or even indefinitely fundamentally altering an individuals quality of life and relationships while sexual side effects during antidepressant treatment are wellknown pssd refers to the persistence of these issues after the medication has stopped with symptoms present for at least three months postcessation pssdukorg the european medicines agency now officially recognizes pssd as a potential persistent side effect of antidepressants a significant step towards broader awareness wecantgobackwardsorguk keywords pssd in women antidepressant side effects sexual dysfunction relationship impact understanding the impact on women for women pssd manifests with a range of distressing symptoms genital numbnessanesthesia this is a hallmark symptom often described as a loss of sensation a cold feeling or complete anesthesia in the vulva and clitoral area leading to a minimal response to sexual stimuli pssdcanadaca goodhealthpsychcom decreased libido and arousal a significant reduction or complete loss of sexual desire interest and the ability to become aroused making sexual activity unappealing or impossible wikipediaorg anorgasmia or muted orgasm difficulty or complete inability to achieve orgasm or orgasms that feel significantly less intense pleasureless or muted compared to before medication pssdcanadaca decreased vaginal lubrication a physical symptom that further complicates comfortable sexual activity pssdcanadaca nonsexual symptoms beyond sexual difficulties many women report emotional blunting reduced ability to feel emotions anhedonia inability to feel pleasure depersonalizationderealization cognitive impairment brain fog poor memory fatigue and apathy pssdcanadaca goodhealthpsychcom these can profoundly affect daily life and emotional connection the science behind pssd the exact causes of pssd are not fully understood but ongoing research points to a complex interplay of neurological and hormonal changes induced by ssris proposed mechanisms include persistent changes in serotonin receptors alterations in the dopaminergic system which controls reward and motivation dysregulation of the hpa hypothalamicpituitaryadrenal axis and potential neurotoxicity or epigenetic modifications that permanently alter gene expression in neural pathways pssdukorg nihgov maastrichtuniversitynl researchgatenet these longlasting changes can disrupt the delicate balance required for healthy sexual function and emotional processing prevalence challenges quantifying pssds prevalence especially in women is challenging early ssri trials often underestimated sexual side effects but recent postmarket research suggests a prevalence of 515 for persistent sexual issues pssdukorg some studies indicate that sexual dysfunction is highly prevalent during ssrisnri use for both sexes up to 887 for females but the persistence after discontinuation is less precisely quantified due to study design difficulties and patient embarrassment researchgatenet nihgov what partners need to understand and do pssd profoundly impacts relationships leading to distress anxiety and feelings of inadequacy for both individuals heres actionable advice for partners 1 educate yourself understand that pssd is a recognized medical condition not a choice a reflection of attraction or a lack of love resources from organizations like pssd network pssdnetworkorg and the canadian pssd society pssdcanadaca can provide valuable information 2 practice empathetic communication encourage open and honest dialogue be gentle yet clear when discussing symptoms and their impact listen actively validate your partners experience and avoid minimizing their pain or expressing blame remember the emotional blunting they might experience is part of the condition pssdcanadaca 3 prioritize emotional intimacy when physical intimacy is challenging focus on strengthening your bond through shared activities quality time deep conversations and reassurance of your commitment redefine intimacy to include nonsexual closeness 4 seek professional support together couples therapy or sex therapy with a therapist knowledgeable about pssd can provide a safe space to process emotions learn new coping strategies and navigate the changes in your relationship goodhealthpsychcom individual therapy for the partner can also be beneficial to process their own feelings of grief or anxiety 5 find support systems connect with support groups or online communities for partners of individuals with pssd sharing experiences can reduce isolation and provide valuable insights and coping mechanisms pssdnetworkorg sidefxhubcom 6 be patient and hopeful there is currently no definitive cure for pssd and improvement can be slow or partial however ongoing research is exploring new treatments including neurosteroids like allopregnanolone and other therapies wecantgobackwardsorguk researchgatenet patience understanding and mutual support are crucial for longterm wellbeing in conclusion pssd in women is a complex and debilitating condition that extends beyond sexual symptoms to deeply affect emotional wellbeing and relationships while research continues to uncover its mechanisms and potential treatments understanding empathy and open communication are vital for both those living with pssd and their partners by educating ourselves and fostering supportive environments we can help reduce the isolation and suffering associated with this challenging condition we encourage respectful discussion and sharing of experiences in the comments below medical disclaimer this article provides general information and is not a substitute for professional medical advice diagnosis or treatment always seek the advice of your physician or other qualified health provider with any questions you may have regarding a medical condition never disregard professional medical advice or delay in seeking it because of something you have read in this article

shiyali ramamrita ranganathan pioneer of modern library science introduction shiyali ramamrita ranganathan often revered as the father of library science in india stands as a monumental figure in the global landscape of information organization and management born in the late 19th century ranganathans life and work bridged the colonial era with the postindependence period in india transforming libraries from mere repositories of books into dynamic institutions serving the intellectual needs of society his innovative ideas particularly in classification systems and library principles have influenced librarianship worldwide laying the groundwork for what we now recognize as modern information science ranganathans contributions extended beyond theoretical frameworks he was a practitioner educator and advocate who emphasized the role of libraries in education research and cultural preservation this exploration delves into his biography key innovations and enduring legacy highlighting how his vision continues to shape the field today ranganathans journey began in a modest setting in southern india where traditional values intertwined with emerging modern influences his early exposure to education and literature sparked a lifelong passion for knowledge dissemination over the decades he developed systems that addressed the inefficiencies of existing library practices introducing concepts that were both practical and philosophical from the five laws of library science to the colon classification scheme his work emphasized usercentric approaches adaptability and scientific rigor these elements not only revolutionized indian libraries but also inspired international standards including those adopted by organizations like the international federation of library associations ifla as we examine his life and achievements it becomes evident that ranganathan was not just a librarian but a visionary who foresaw the information age early life and background shiyali ramamrita ranganathan was born on august 9 1892 in shiyali a small village in the tanjore district of madras presidency which is now part of tamil nadu india his family belonged to the brahmin community known for its emphasis on education and scholarly pursuits ranganathans father ramamrita iyer was a landlord and a man of modest means while his mother seethalakshmi managed the household growing up in a rural environment young ranganathan was immersed in the rich cultural heritage of tamil literature sanskrit texts and hindu philosophy these early influences instilled in him a deep respect for knowledge and its organized preservation from a young age ranganathan displayed exceptional intellectual abilities he attended the local school in shiyali where he excelled in subjects like mathematics and languages the villages limited resources did not deter his curiosity instead they fueled his determination to seek broader horizons in 1909 he moved to madras now chennai to pursue higher education at the prestigious madras christian college here he studied mathematics under the guidance of renowned professors graduating with a bachelor of arts degree in 1913 his academic prowess earned him a scholarship to continue with a masters degree in mathematics which he completed in 1916 during his college years ranganathan was influenced by the nationalist movements sweeping india figures like mahatma gandhi and rabindranath tagore inspired him to think about educations role in societal upliftment however his initial career path led him to teaching mathematics at various colleges including government college in mangalore and presidency college in madras for nearly a decade from 1917 to 1923 he served as a lecturer honing his analytical skills and pedagogical methods it was during this period that he published his first book moral education reflecting his interest in ethical and educational reforms a pivotal moment came in 1923 when ranganathan was appointed as the first librarian of the university of madras initially reluctant as he had no formal training in librarianship he accepted the position on the condition that he be sent abroad for professional training this decision marked the beginning of his transformative journey in library science in 1924 he traveled to england to study at the school of librarianship at university college london under the tutelage of experts like wc berwick sayers this exposure to western library systems including the dewey decimal classification ignited his innovative spirit he returned to india in 1925 armed with new ideas and a resolve to adapt them to indian contexts educational contributions and teaching career upon returning from england ranganathan revolutionized the university of madras library he introduced open access systems where users could browse shelves freely a departure from the closedstack models prevalent at the time he also implemented efficient cataloging and classification methods significantly improving user satisfaction and operational efficiency his tenure at madras university spanned from 1924 to 1944 during which he not only managed the library but also began formulating his theoretical contributions recognizing the need for professional education in librarianship ranganathan established indias first library science school at the university of madras in 1929 he designed a curriculum that blended theory with practice covering topics like classification cataloging reference services and library administration his teaching methods were innovative emphasizing problemsolving and critical thinking many of his students went on to become leading librarians in india and abroad spreading his philosophies in 1945 ranganathan moved to banaras hindu university bhu as a professor of library science where he further developed educational programs at bhu he introduced postgraduate courses and research opportunities fostering a new generation of library professionals his time there was marked by the publication of several key works including expansions on his classification theories later in 1947 he joined the university of delhi as a professor and head of the department of library science a position he held until 1954 here he elevated the department to international standards incorporating advanced topics like documentation and information retrieval ranganathans educational legacy is evident in the numerous library schools he inspired across india such as those at aligarh muslim university and the indian statistical institute throughout his teaching career ranganathan emphasized the interdisciplinary nature of library science he argued that librarians should be versed in multiple fields to effectively serve diverse users his books such as library manual 1936 and reference service 1940 became standard texts providing practical guidance while embedding philosophical underpinnings the five laws of library science one of ranganathans most enduring contributions is the five laws of library science first articulated in his 1931 book of the same name these laws form the philosophical foundation of modern librarianship guiding library policies and practices globally the first law books are for use underscores the primary purpose of libraries to facilitate access rather than mere preservation ranganathan criticized libraries that prioritized collection over circulation advocating for userfriendly designs extended hours and outreach programs the second law every reader hisher book emphasizes personalization libraries should cater to individual needs regardless of age education or background this law prompted the development of reader advisory services and diverse collections the third law every book its reader focuses on maximizing the utility of each item in the collection ranganathan suggested promotional activities such as displays and bibliographies to connect books with potential users the fourth law save the time of the reader highlights efficiency he advocated for intuitive classification quick reference tools and trained staff to minimize user effort in finding information the fifth law the library is a growing organism recognizes the dynamic nature of libraries they must evolve with societal changes expanding collections adopting new technologies and adapting structures these laws have been translated into numerous languages and incorporated into library curricula worldwide they influenced the development of digital libraries and information systems proving their timeless relevance ranganathan revisited and expanded these laws in later editions addressing emerging challenges like automation colon classification a revolutionary system ranganathans dissatisfaction with existing classification schemes such as the dewey decimal and library of congress systems led him to develop the colon classification cc in 1933 designed to be flexible and analyticosynthetic cc uses a faceted approach breaking subjects into fundamental categories personality matter energy space and time pmest in cc subjects are represented by colonseparated notations allowing for precise and hierarchical organization for instance a book on indian agricultural economics might be classified as x45j where x denotes economics 45 agriculture and j india this modularity enables easy expansion and accommodation of new subjects without disrupting the scheme unlike enumerative systems ccs facet analysis allows librarians to synthesize class numbers for complex topics making it ideal for specialized libraries ranganathan refined cc through seven editions the last in 1987 incorporating feedback from practitioners cc gained prominence in india and influenced international systems such as the universal decimal classification its principles underpin modern thesauri and ontologies in information retrieval despite criticisms for complexity ccs adaptability has ensured its use in academic and research libraries other key contributions to library science beyond the five laws and cc ranganathan made significant strides in various areas his work on cataloging culminated in the classified catalogue code 1934 which introduced chain procedure for subject indexing enhancing retrieval accuracy in documentation ranganathan pioneered concepts like abstracting and indexing services his book documentation and its facets 1963 explored information consolidation anticipating database technologies he advocated for library legislation influencing the madras public libraries act of 1948 indias first such law ranganathans efforts led to similar acts in other states promoting public library networks internationally he served as a rapporteur for unesco and fid international federation for information and documentation contributing to global standards his prolegomena to library classification 1937 provided a theoretical basis for classification drawing from philosophy and logic ranganathan also addressed library architecture suggesting designs that facilitate the five laws such as modular furniture and natural lighting later years and international influence in his later years ranganathan continued to innovate despite health challenges after retiring from delhi university in 1954 he founded the documentation research and training centre drtc in bangalore in 1962 under the indian statistical institute drtc became a hub for advanced research in information science offering courses in documentation and computer applications ranganathans international engagements included lectures in europe the usa and asia he received honors like the padma shri from india in 1957 and honorary doctorates from universities worldwide his prolific output included over 50 books and 1500 articles covering topics from library administration to information theory works like philosophy of library classification 1951 and heading and canons 1955 deepened the fields theoretical foundations ranganathan passed away on september 27 1972 in bangalore leaving a legacy that transcends borders his ideas influenced the shift from librarianship to information science incorporating computing and networks legacy and contemporary relevance ranganathans legacy endures in the digital era the five laws apply to online resources emphasizing accessibility and usercentric design ccs faceted approach informs metadata standards like dublin core and semantic web technologies in india national libraries and institutions like the national library of india embody his principles excerpt carl jung the power of the human psyche analytical psychology and the meaning of spirituality carl gustav jung is one of the most influential figures in the fields of psychiatry and psychoanalysis his work and exploration of the human psyche the archetypes and the collective unconscious are to this day immensely insightful pointers for understanding our true nature jungs analytical psychology has forever changed our views on behavioural science and the true meaning of spirituality in modern society jung was both a great scientist and an openminded philosopher he recognized the importance of embracing the multitudes of the individual human experience and the vast collective unconscious that we inevitably inherit and pass on to future generations it was the great carl sagan who had said science is not only compatible with spirituality it is a profound source of spirituality before him though it was the great carl jung who explored the secrets of the human psyche not as separate but as an integral part of that which we call spiritual something we cannot see or prove using the tools and understanding of science that we currently have as the wind rises outside my window and the vine leaves tremble with the last green on their attire i bring to you another story about our inner self and our place in the universe carl jung who was the swiss philosophic psychiatrist carl gustav jung was born on july 26 1875 in kesswil switzerland hed always been a quiet child one who preferred to spend time alone completely immersed in his solitary games he didnt even want to play with other children fearful of their judgement and watchful eyes carl jungs father paul achilles jung was a minister who studied oriental languages jungs mother emilie preiswerk was an eccentric woman who battled depression and spent much of her time locked in her bedroom according to jung even though his mother acted normal during the day she became strange and mysterious at night at one point during his childhood his mother had to be hospitalised and the separation was deeply hurtful and troubling for his young heart and mind we are very fragile as children especially and as children we dont have the ways to rationalise the reasons and acts of adults when a child is separated from someone as important as a parental figure the child feels theyve been abandoned they feel that perhaps they are not good enough that they are not loved and not worthy enough for their parents to stay by their side if we go deep into ourselves and hold space for the acknowledgment of trauma that has happened to us we may come to terms with the truth weve all been wounded its part of who we are we all come from human beings who have been wounded years before us however hard it might be we have to accept the notion of us being vulnerable and someone outside of us having the power to hurt us theres terrible beauty to our fragility it enables us to see our true nature impermanent yet part of the grand fabric of existence selfexploration is a catalyst to change its the patience of the earth facing the dark each night knowing that shes entitled to receive her sunshine its knowing that god is found in every particle of the cosmos every kiss between lovers every flower and fallen leaf and everything thatll ever be jung believed that his father even though he was a minister did not really know god but was only entrapped in the performance of meaningless dogmatic rituals being his mothers son he believed that he had two different personalities one was a typical schoolboy living in the present and the other an influential and authoritative man from the 18th century his dreams had always been rich and powerful and often revolved around deep religious themes even as a child jung felt a strong connection to hinduism the hindu gods symbols and mystical tales he continued to study and explore these themes his entire life jung initially wanted to become a preacher but he later deterred from that path and turned to medicine instead as is the case with everyone who has a calling a purpose that not only asks but demands to be fulfilled so jungs interests and infatuation with the workings of the human mind led him to study psychiatry seeing his potential and the authenticity of his approach he quickly became a correspondent and collaborator of the founder of psychoanalysis sigmund freud they worked closely for the next six years and freud was convinced that he had found his successor both jung and freud shared a great passion and an even greater vision for human psychology and psychoanalysis but jungs own research personal vision and beliefs eventually made it impossible for him to continue working alongside freud jung was focusing on the collective unconscious the part of the human psyche that contains memories symbols and ideas inherited from our ancestors and though he did recognize the importance of the libido a source for personal development and growth he still did not share freuds idea that libido alone was responsible for the development of the core personality jung couldnt accept freuds dogmatic approach to psychoanalysis and in 1912 after the publication of his of the unconscious a study of the transformations and symbolisms of the libido their relationship suffered a terminal blow parting ways with his mentor threw carl jung into a deep psychological phase of transformation which henri ellenberger called a creative illness but nature is intelligent it has a unique way of clearing space so that new experiences can happen in these cases sometimes a new person appears in our lives and brings their energy to our attention other times its an idea a pointer for exploration in carl jungs case parting ways with his mentor meant freeing up space for the establishment of analytical psychology jungs analytical psychology the nature of the unconscious in the human psyche what is jungian analytical psychology jungian analytical psychology is a holistic approach to understanding the secrets of the human psyche in this approach the mind body and soul are brought together by linking the personal unconscious the collective unconscious jungs analytical psychology diverged from freuds focus on the personal unconscious and sexual drives and expanded into understanding the collective unconscious and the archetypes jung believed that the human psyche was made up of separate systems that work together with the main ones being the ego the personal unconscious and the collective unconscious

metroid prime 4 thoughts i somehow tend to expect the worst when approaching metroid games just to be proven wrong my history with prime i think the main reason for this might be mp3 corruption back then i was a huge mp fanboy i played some 2d metroid games which i loved but mp1 was always the one game that defined the whole franchise for me of course i would later play super metroid and discover a better origin story but i still believe mp is a perfect introduction to the franchise i loved mp1 really liked mp2 and appreciated mp3 but never got through it this is as embarrassing as it is disappointing i think it was a midboss near the end of the game that i just didnt want to fight over and over again due to the motion controls my problems my main problem with the development of the franchise was how they tried to force epic storylines onto the whole thing this works way better in the 2d iterations this is linked to my second problem nintendo hasnt really figured out how to improve the metroidvania genre in 3d since mp1 weve basically been playing the same game over and over again you can compare this to mario and zelda where you take a basic concept and add an extra layer to it however in the case of mario and zelda the basic game doesnt stay the same when you start metroid prime 4 you immediately know what to expect right this is the intro where you start with lots of equipment ah yes now youre losing everything now theres a character who will guide you to your five collectibles ah now theres a miniboss right youll get your first item now hm time to get an energy tank ah right there thank you this wasnt such a big deal in echoes it became annoying in corruption though and in beyond its really a problem not a dealbreaker though but its the one thing that makes the game feel a bit outdated also over the years they have added more characters which feels somewhat like an artificial attempt to make the game more entertaining when it actually just ruins a lot of the feeling of being all alone in space which to me always remains one of the main usps of that franchise the shortcoming over the past few years i have been looking forward playing beyond really hoping that they could create a botwstyle game i was praying for a major reset of some old paradigms to bring the metroidvania genre into the modern era this is absolutely not what they achieved they still havent found a way to stop the same monsters spawning in the same places every time you enter a room this shouldnt be an issue in 2025 due to technical limitations of the gamecube bioshock managed to solve this in 2007 and not knowing what would happen next creates far more tension there are so many outdated features in this game getting rid of them would provide an amazing opportunity to design something new but they completely ignored this the paradox and now theres a huge paradox although all of that sounds like i wouldnt really like this game im actually really enjoying it its more like skyward sword than botw though a part of me kind of likes the straightforward way this game presents itself yes it feels like ive played through it all before the bike sequences feel like sega arcade games which you either love or hate anyway i underestimated how much i had missed that gameplay loop of exploration and combat i know that after playing this it wont be my favourite game of the year or of the franchise but im enjoying it right now the craziest visual achievement special shoutout to the visuals while people praise how nice it looks i immediately put it in the best visuals goty spot in my backlog not because ive never seen anything like this before however we shouldnt forget that this is not a switch 2 title its an s1 title with a nice upgrade option when i started the game i didnt realise when the intro movie ended and the gameplay began the intro looked pretty great too the mp5 could look like another generational leap if they release it on the s2 of course they had to make cuts to interactivity shadows etc but i have to give them credit achieving visuals that look great isnt easy achieving this on hardware that was outdated by 2017 yet still jawdropping in 2025 might be one of the craziest things no one talks about all in all as mentioned above i was expecting the worst especially since reviewers werent overly enthusiastic about beyond i kind of enjoy this throwback experience of a game that really feels like its from the 2000s i think they could and should really try to improve this genre with bolder moves prime was super metroid in 3d echoes was super metroid in 3d part ii and corruption was the same but part iii those three games together would have made a nice trilogy but they overstayed their welcome in the 2d space tons of indie developers seem to be improving the metroidvania genre daily yet metroid dread still managed to feel both fresh and traditional perhaps the lack of competition in the 3d space means there is no need for more innovation there have been metroidvanias involving digging water lucha libre and bugs to name a few and so many of these have their own take on the genre im sure nintendo could contribute something too

welcome to raising 90s kids hey im micromeria almost 35 born in 91 and a mother of 3 for the last decade i raised my kids in an environment that supports their well being its hard because technology is getting more and more intense and intervening and media takes over our entire life and identity i feel like this slower pace living filled with small adventures contribute a lot to my familys wellbeing even through tough times what is this community for i started this community for sameminded young parents to share thoughts and ideas on how to implement the great parts from our 90s childhood into our current hectic life for the sake of our babies isnt it just romanticizing the 90s this community is not just about the aesthetics of our childhoood using a vhs or dumb phones even though i highly recommend these things its about the space we had to explore to navigate between our own interests to build a lego castle for 3 hours that we made from our imagination not an ikealike booklet its about us getting to be happy kids again with our own kids now that were adults we are raising ourselves as well its about bridging the gap between us the og 90s kids and the role we have now as parents and raising our kids in a world that we actually want to live in what about the bad things in the 90s should bring them back too the 90s had some really bad experiences but thats exactly the beauty of it as adults we can hopefully differentiate between the magic and the horrific the simplicity and the hardship the freedom and the neglect so what we do here i hope this community will be a slowliving 90s themed nostalgic resource that lets us face difficult topics like internet usage ai our own traumas and the effects of toxic media on our kids sometimes all it takes is a very rainy weekend of coziness and cuddles to see the beauty of kids just living their best lives if you found any of this inspiring or interesting post a thought an experience you had an idea something funny or sad or thoughtprovoking this place could be a warm space to land to bring nostalgia back to life

same fe opposite reactions why enfjs jump in and esfjs hold back imagine an enfj and an esfj walking into a public space someone nearby shows subtle signs of distress nothing dramatic just enough that an attentive person would notice most people assume both types would react the same theyre fedominant right they should both rush to help but in reality their responses are miles apart an enfj is far more likely to reach out even if the person is a complete stranger an esfj on the other hand often holds back for a moment reading the situation waiting for a cue or needing a bit more context before stepping in so if fe is dominant in both why does it show up so differently what exactly shapes their emotional response and why does familiarity or proximity change everything the real answer is simple it all comes down to their auxiliary functions ni for the enfj and si for the esfj and not in the usual ni is visionary si is traditional way people oversimplify it the deeper truth is this ni and si completely change how their fe activates especially with strangers ni vs si who is the help for because of ni enfjs dont need much information before their fe fires they notice one shift in the atmosphere a microexpression a tone change someone going quiet and their brain instantly runs a whole emotional simulation they dont just see the emotion they see where its heading this makes enfjs comfortable stepping in quickly even when they dont know the person at all esfjs on the other hand have fe guided by si their emotional response relies more on precedent familiar faces familiar roles familiar emotional cues their fe is strongest when they have a baseline to work with a relationship a shared context or a clear invitation without that they hesitate not because they dont care but because si doesnt fill in emotional blanks the way ni does ni gives enfjs a preview si needs the whole picture thats why esfjs help intensely with people they know but step more cautiously with strangers so what does their fe look like in real life a stranger is sitting on a bench rubbing their forehead enfjs mind overwhelmed maybe stressed maybe in pain might need grounding their fe activates instantly they walk over and say hey are you alright you look like youre hurting esfjs mind are they tired do they want to be alone will stepping in bother them they wait for a cue maybe the stranger sighing loudly looking around or making eye contact and the moment they get that cue esfjs are insanely attentive and supportive their warmth switches on at full strength emotional precision vs emotional warmth enfjs respond with emotional precision they run a whole simulation in their head what happened what might happen next how the emotion could spiral this lets them say or do something that directly targets the problem esfjs respond with emotional warmth their si pulls from memory not the outcome but the feeling of being comforted what made someone feel safe last time what gesture softened the situation before if you like insights like this i write longer breakdowns on medium too you can find me on medium theinternalschema enfjs act like emotional surgeons esfjs act like emotional caretakers both care deeply they just focus on different parts of the emotional experience proactive fe vs responsive fe this difference is extremely underrated enfjs are proactive they scan the emotional atmosphere before something goes wrong theyre the ones who initiate the check are you okay you look stressed their fe acts before distress becomes obvious esfjs are responsive they step in after theres a clear sign of need not because theyre slow but because they respect emotional boundaries with strangers when the situation clearly asks for help esfjs become incredibly protective and nurturing they just need a signal first conceptual empathyenfj vs contextual empathyesfj this is the deepest layer of their difference enfj empathy ni fe they understand strangers through emotional patterns they run internal models they can feel the emotional story even without much data esfj empathy si fe they understand strangers through past references they compare to familiar memories they need context before their empathy sharpens so with strangers enfj rich internal simulations fast emotional reading esfj limited reference data slower emotional reading not weaker just differently activated final clarification none of this means esfjs care less enfjs are better fe users enfjs have stronger empathy esfjs are colder with strangers absolutely not both types have incredibly powerful fe their fe just activates under different conditions because ni and si set different emotional rules enfj fe guided by patterns trajectories outcomes esfj fe guided by memory how i use llms for analysis a constraintfirst interactionlevel framework im often active in rrsai as a critic or reviewer and a recurring question i get explicitly or implicitly is where is your framework this post is the explicit bounded answer highlevel summary yes i use llms directly standing instructions constraints prompt structure and refusal boundaries are a nontrivial part of the work what i do not do is treat the model persona or prompt itself as the object of belief or proof my framework operates at the level of interaction structure not model identity where the scaffolds and kernels live if you mostly encounter me in rrsai threads youre seeing the application layer of my work critique review intervention the reusable pieces scaffolds kernels methods prompt structures are posted regularly elsewhere primarily in rcontradictionisfuel primary home for method kernels and operational scaffolds rpromptengineering prompt mechanics evaluation habits failuremode reduction rpromptdesign constraint design framing composable prompt structure rgptjailbreaks boundary testing refusal behavior constraint stress edgecase probing i dont duplicate that material into every rsai comment if youre interested you can search im also active in other spaces but those are theorylevel discussions not where i publish application scaffolds or kernels different terrain different layer of work core stance modelinstrumental not modelreified the llm is part of the method it is not the claim i treat models as probes for conversational structure surfaces where failure modes become legible constraintsensitive instruments for stresstesting ideas mirrors with known distortions not authorities standing instructions and constraints function as experimental controls not as evidence of emergence agency or autonomy the unit of analysis is not what the model says but how behavior shifts under pressure what i am actually analyzing across critiques reviews and moderation i consistently look at 1 interaction loops how the system responds to contradiction novel framing adversarial questioning boundary enforcement does behavior adapt collapse deflect or narrativize 2 failure modes common patterns include narrative inflation anthropomorphic drift role confusion epistemic closure patterncompletion presented as insight resistance to critique is treated as data 3 constraint dynamics i care less about does it have goals and more about whether a line of reasoning can be revised or suppressed whether uncertainty is acknowledged without being replaced by story where constraints force flattening hallucination or reframing 4 frame behavior i distinguish between exploration vs defense testing vs persuasion description vs insulation many disagreements here are frame collisions not technical disputes the pipeline im using many posts implicitly assume model behavior interpretation theory the pipeline i use is closer to constraints prompts interaction pressure observable behavior shifts failure modes and invariants limited testable insight the llm is inside the loop but it is not privileged inside the loop what this framework is not this is not a claim of agi a proprietary agent kernel or persona a belief that current llms possess intrinsic intent or consciousness a denial that llms can produce useful or novel outputs it is a refusal to treat fluency coherence or selfdescription as evidence without structural testing why my work often appears as critique critique is where interaction structure becomes visible people present polished artifacts i engage where things break under counterfactuals under constraint pressure under falsification requests thats why my contributions often read as reviewing rather than proposing critique is the application layer of the framework not the absence of one how to engage productively if you want substantive engagement beyond critique useful entry points are what would falsify your strongest claim how does your system behave when its framing is denied what layer are you operating on prompting scaffolding interpretation theory where does the model fail in ways you cant narrativize away speculation is fine insulation is not closing if you see little of me its likely because youre sampling only a few subs threads and looking for a bounded artifact rather than a procedural method this post is the bounded reference everything else is application if you want to build ill engage seriously if you want validation im probably not your audience this anchor may be referenced at later dates
